about: Thresholds, word lists and flag rules for the portfolio overview. scripts/portfolio_health.py reads this file and its CLI defaults come from it; change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes, and references/health-checks.md says what each flag means.

notes.min_customers: A project with events but fewer customers than this is flagged small_customer_base. Lower it for portfolios of small brands.
notes.min_event_types: A project tracking fewer event types than this (from the overview's event_types_overview) is flagged few_event_types: tracking may be partial.
notes.min_projects_for_median: Outlier flags are only raised when at least this many comparable projects (not test or sandbox, with events) exist; with fewer, a median means little.
notes.outlier_low_ratio: A comparable project whose customers, or events per customer, are below this fraction of the portfolio median is flagged outlier_low.
notes.outlier_high_ratio: A comparable project whose events per customer are above this multiple of the portfolio median is flagged outlier_high: duplicate or bot tracking is worth a look.
notes.shrink_ratio: With --baseline, a project whose customer count fell by more than this fraction since the baseline is flagged shrinking_customers. Events that fell at all are flagged fewer_events (retention or deletion).
notes.sandbox_categories: Project categories (compared case-insensitively) that count as sandbox or test. Seen values include int, sandbox and none.
notes.test_name_words: Whole words in a project's name or URL slug that make it look like a test, sandbox or demo project. Matched as words, so 'contest' doesn't match 'test'.
notes.system_event_types: Event types the platform records itself (campaign sends, weblayer views, consent changes). They're left out when picking a project's busiest event types for busy_types_silent, because they don't show that site or app tracking works.
notes.busy_event_types: In deeper mode, this many of a project's busiest non-system event types (by all-time count) are checked for events in the last 7 days. Any that are silent raise busy_types_silent.
notes.recent_top_n: The N in the deeper-mode query 'grouping top N'. If the query returns N rows, event types missing from it may just be cut off, so busy_types_silent isn't judged.
notes.max_deep_projects: Deeper mode runs on at most this many projects in one go, lowest scores first. Say the call count and ask before going further.
notes.deep_calls_per_project: Calls deeper mode makes per project (an EQL cost estimate, the EQL query and one active-scenario list), used to tell the user the call count first.
notes.score_green: A health score at or above this is green.
notes.score_amber: A health score at or above this (and below score_green) is amber; below it is red.
notes.max_scenarios_page: The page size used for the active-scenario list in deeper mode. A page this full is reported as 'this many or more'.
notes.flags: Every flag the script can raise: how many points it takes off the health score (which starts at 100 and stops at 0), its priority (high, medium or low) and the skill to hand the project to. test_or_sandbox, overview_unavailable and events_unknown take nothing off: they explain a score, they don't lower it. This is the only place hand-offs are defined; the script's handoffs output groups flagged projects by them.
